title: Replication lag and read-your-writes

kcs.statement: Replication lag is the delay between a write committing on the leader and appearing on a follower, so a read served by a follower can return stale data.
To give a user read-your-writes, route that user's reads to the leader for a short window after they write, or until the follower has applied that write.

problem_ideas: A user edits their bio and refreshes 300 ms later; lag is 1 s: predict what they see and fix it
Lag spikes to 30 s during a batch import: list which features break
Design a rule that routes reads to the leader for 5 seconds after a write; estimate the extra leader load
A user sees a comment, refreshes, and it disappears: explain with two replicas at different lag
Pick which reads in a banking app must never go to a follower
Lag is 200 ms on average and 4 s at p99: decide whether a cache in front changes the staleness story
